newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end lower, marks hit new low.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end lower, marks hit new low.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mostly lower, with June marks and Canadian dollars each sagging during the final minutes to a new contract low.
June marks slipped to their low at $0.5804 after punching below the previous low of $0.5815, about 1.7274 spot, and triggering sell stops.
Nearby Canadian dollars peeked below the old contract low at $0.7176 and hit $0.7174 during the final hour.
Brokers said impetus for the final leg down likely was the dash higher in U.S. stocks after Friday's slide. U.S. Treasury bond futures, however, stayed stuck little changed on the day.

But they also said order flows stayed sparse even on the break down before more U.S. economic data this week, amid uncertainty about possible central bank intervention and edginess about whether U.S. asset markets will fall further.
Exchange price boards showed estimated volume in nearby marks and Canadian dollars at only 11,000 and 3,000 contracts, respectively.

"It's dead as can be at the lows of the day," said one floor broker. "I hate to say it, but we need a dollar selloff to get busy again. People are long of dollars and people who don't have a position aren't going to buy (dollars) up here."
Afternoon comments by U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin had little effect, floor brokers said.

Rubin said U.S. dollar policy remains the same, and he declined comment on any foreign exchange intervention plan. Rubin also repeated that Japan should seek demand-led growth and avoid a significant rise in its current account surplus.
The possibility of intervention to brake the dollar's rise continued to loom, although some said dollar selling by the Bank of Japan alone might not derail the dollar's rally.
A floor broker, asked if traders think intervention by the BOJ would succeed, replied, "By themselves? Nobody."

They waited to see if March's U.S consumer price index Tuesday would jar beliefs that U.S. rates will head higher soon. CPI on average is forecast rising 0.2 percent and gaining 0.3 percent in the core rate.
Some traders already looked to the spring meeting of International Monetary Fund, World Bank and Group of Seven bankers and finance ministers April 23-29 in Washington, DC.

June yen lost $0.000029 to $0.007981, marks lost $0.0029 to $0.5809, Swiss franc fell $0.0036 to $0.6854, sterling fell $0.0068 to $1.6200, Can dollar eased $0.0003 to $0.7175, Aussie dollar lost $0.0051 to $0.7791, M.peso off $0.000150 at $0.122425.
